resources.string: TV Debloater talks to your Android TV over Wi-Fi using ADB. Do this once on the TV with the remote:
Select \"Build\" (Build number) and press OK 7 times until you see \"You are now a developer\".
Go back to Device Preferences > Developer options and turn the Developer options switch on.
Turn on \"USB debugging\". If you see \"Network debugging\" or \"ADB over network\", turn it on too.
Find the TV\'s IP address: Settings > Network & Internet > select your Wi-Fi network. It looks like 192.168.1.23.
Keep the phone and the TV on the same Wi-Fi network.
Nothing runs without your confirmation. Dry run is on by default, so you will first only see the commands. Every change is saved and can be undone.
Look at the TV now: it shows \"Allow USB debugging?\". Tick \"Always allow from this computer\" and press OK. Waiting up to 90 seconds.
No device with an open port was found. Check that debugging is on, or type the IP manually.
The phone is not on Wi-Fi. Connect it to the same Wi-Fi as the TV.
The TV did not answer in time. Check the IP address and that both devices are on the same Wi-Fi.
The TV did not confirm the connection. Did you press OK on the \"Allow USB debugging?\" prompt on the TV? Try again and accept it.
The TV refused the connection on this port. Turn on USB debugging / network debugging in Developer options and try again.
The TV cannot be reached at this address. Check the IP address in the TV\'s network settings.
The TV rejected this phone (unauthorized). Retry and press OK on the TV prompt. If no prompt appears, open Developer options > Revoke USB debugging authorisations, then retry.
The connection to the TV was lost. Changes made so far are saved in History.
Not connected. Connect to the TV first.
Not in the database (unverified). Treated as CAUTION.
Unknown Android core package. Protected to be safe.

This also preselects some CAUTION packages (recommendations, PatchWall, Mi Cast, contacts/calendar storage). Some TV features may stop working. You can review and untick anything before confirming, and undo everything from History.
Reading the package list from the TV…
Dry run is ON: commands are only shown, nothing changes on the TV. Turn it off in Settings.
Fills the app with sample data so you can try every screen without a TV. Nothing is sent to any device. Disconnect to leave demo mode.
None of the selected packages can take this action.
Nothing to restore: everything this app changed is already enabled.
Remove %1$d packages for the current user?
These exact commands will be sent to the TV:
Dry run is ON: nothing will be executed.
Contains CAUTION packages. Some features may stop working.

\"Remove for current user\" hides the app for user 0. The APK stays on the system and can be brought back with \"Restore\" (cmd package install-existing). A factory reset also brings it back. Its data for this user is kept (-k), but prefer \"Disable\" if you are unsure.
Skipped (already in that state or not allowed): %1$s
Dry run: %1$d commands shown, nothing executed.

Restart the TV yourself when convenient (Settings > Device Preferences > About > Restart) so the changes fully apply. Wait about a minute after the last change before restarting. The app never restarts the TV.
No changes yet. Every real batch is saved here before it runs.
Re-enables every package this app has ever disabled or removed (from History).
Show the exact commands without executing them.
Language follows the phone\'s system language (Turkish or English).
No ads, no analytics. The app only talks to the TV on your local network. Package classifications come from public Mi TV Stick (MDZ-24-AA) debloat lists; unknown packages are treated as CAUTION.

1) Use History > Undo, or Restore all. 2) Restart the TV. 3) If the TV no longer boots, factory reset it: unplug it, hold OK + Back on the remote while plugging the power back in, then choose Wipe data / factory reset, or use Settings > Device Preferences > Reset. A factory reset brings back every system app.
